Event: we participated in the 2026 TravelDaily Conference held in Shanghai on Sept. 22-23. The two-day conference and exhibition content included: (1) AI applications in the travel industry; (2) this year's market conditions and future increments of the travel industry; (3) hotel groups' growth strategies.   
Regarding AI applications in the travel industry, we believe that the core conclusions from the conference are mainly the following: 1) AI penetration rate has increased notably and still has room, as only 8% of transactions are conducted through AI. 2) AI agents in hotels & tourism have already crossed the usability line and begun to enter the "transaction closed loop", and AI travel has also begun to enter the execution-layer competition; 3) the traffic entry point shifts from SEO to GEO; Meituan has established a dedicated GEO department, and Marriott is cooperating with AI companies to ensure official content is crawled; 4) OTA platforms are all laying out AI, but with different approaches and rhythms; Fliggy connects with the Alibaba ecosystem, to C\to B\to organization; Meituan bets heavily on the merchant side, focusing on the data layer + strategy layer + execution layer. 4) On whether AI can reconstruct the travel industry, Emerging Travel Group believes AI will change the transaction entry point but will not remove the middle layer. 
To summarize, the current industry consensus is 1) GEO replaces SEO; 2) B-end supply chain and fulfillment capabilities cannot be disrupted; 3) AI implementation depends on the income statement; 4) Human-machine division of labor in service (AI manages standardization, humans manage trust and exceptions); 5) The industry is in an early window period. However, industry divergences lie in 1) whether AI can directly complete transactions: Visiotrip/Fliggy/Meituan are relatively positive (having built real-time verification and one-click booking), while Fosun/Hong Kong Airlines are cautious (users will still return to the platform to compare prices); 2) whether AI is a threat or complementary to OTA: Marriott's CEO believes that AI agents will impact OTA more than hotels; Trip.com advocates complementary win-win; Meituan uses "Jibai" to move upward and reconstruct its role; 3) the path of hotel organizational reform: Delonix's radical route of 100% AI-ization vs most hotels merely using basic applications. 
Based on the content of this conference, our view is: AI's reconstruction or diversion of traffic entry points is a high probability, but it is still at an early stage. At this stage, Trip.com still benefits because traffic prices are low; in the longer term, as agent penetration increases, GEO will replace traditional search advertising. At the same time, the boundaries of competition are changing, and future victory or defeat depends on who can enable agents to complete real transactions safely, stably, and in real time. AI is unlikely to replace the middle layer, i.e., OTA, because the transaction network involves content, inventory, dynamic pricing, cancellation policies, taxes and commissions, payment and refunds, customer service and dispute handling, data consistency among multiple suppliers, fulfillment responsibility, etc. The truly valuable middle layer will become the "protocol layer" and "trust layer" in the agent ecosystem. The final competitive landscape is still unclear. Trip.com can rely on its already-formed supply chain scale advantages and fulfillment capabilities, and by cooperating with leading model vendors, consolidate its competitive advantages. But Fliggy and Meituan may participate in competition from the traffic end and supply chain end by providing AI business products to merchants and leveraging their own ecosystems (Taobao, AutoNavi, takeout, Dianping, etc.). 
More details are as follows: 
1） AI penetration in the hotels & tourism industry: the transaction closed loop is the watershed, and AI travel has entered execution-layer competition
 The travel service chain and scenarios have all achieved AI penetration: the traditional service chain of "consultation-planning-booking-payment-fulfillment" has been repackaged by AI into continuous tasks. Verifiable AI products have appeared in the five segments of inspiration, planning, booking, in-transit, and reimbursement. Product representatives are respectively ① Booking & OpenAI's accommodation inspiration; ② Google AI Mode, relying on Gemini, connecting flight, hotel, and map information to generate one-stop itinerary plans; ③ Mindtrip Flights: self-developed agent connecting to Sabre inventory + PayPal, completing flight booking and payment within the conversation; ④ Fly Delta App: built-in generative AI, providing real-time itinerary reminders and travel problem support; ⑤ Navan App: Navan's self-developed agent, processing 27 receipts for reimbursement in only 70 seconds.
